dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5201.text: Obstinate. Formed from 匕 and 目: eyes facing one another, neither yielding. The Changes says: “Keeping his waist still.” 匕 with 目 makes 𥃩; 𠤎 with 目 makes 眞.

shuowen:5202.text: To heed one another. Formed from two 人. All characters in this group are formed from 从.

shuowen:5203.text: To follow along. Formed from 辵 and 从; 从 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5204.text: To accompany one another. Formed from 从, with 幵 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 从 holding two makes 并.

shuowen:5205.text: Close. Two 人 make 从; reversing 从 makes 比. All characters in this group are formed from 比.

shuowen:5206.text: Careful. Formed from 比, with 必 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Do not be cautious only about what causes distress”; the quotation 無毖于卹 is uncertain.

shuowen:5207.text: To turn one’s back. Formed from two people back to back. All characters in this group are formed from 北.

shuowen:5208.text: A northern province. Formed from 北, with 異 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5209.text: A natural rise of earth, not made by people. Formed from 北 and 一; 一 is the ground. People live south of hills, hence 北. The central states lie southeast of Kunlun. Another explanation: high on four sides and low in the middle is 丘. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 丘. The present clerical transformation is 丘.

shuowen:5210.text: A great hill: Kunlun Hill is called Kunlun Xu. In antiquity nine households made a jing, four jing a settlement, four settlements a qiu; a qiu was called xu. Formed from 丘, with 虍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5211.text: A hill with a hollow top receiving water. Formed from 丘, with abbreviated 泥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5212.text: Many people standing. Formed from three 人. All characters in the 乑 group follow 乑. Read like 崟 in 欽崟.

shuowen:5213.text: Many. Formed from 乑 and 目, conveying a multitude.

shuowen:5214.text: To gather. Formed from 乑, with 取 indicating the sound. A settlement is called a 聚.

shuowen:5215.text: The collective connective “and.” Formed from 乑, with 自 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “And Gao Yao.”

shuowen:5216.text: Good. Formed from 人 and 士; 士 means service. Another explanation: depicting things emerging upright from the earth. All characters in this group are formed from 𡈼.

shuowen:5217.text: To summon. Formed from abbreviated 微; 壬 makes it 徵. One whose conduct is unobtrusive but whose learning is accomplished is summoned.

shuowen:5218.text: The full moon facing the sun, as one attends the ruler’s court. Formed from 月, 臣 and 𡈼; 𡈼 represents the court.

shuowen:5219.text: To seek nearby. Formed from 爪 and 𡈼; 𡈼 means seeking good fortune by chance.

shuowen:5220.text: Thick or weighty. Formed from 壬, with 東 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 重.

shuowen:5221.text: To weigh lightness and heaviness. Formed from abbreviated 重, with abbreviated 曏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5222.text: To rest. Formed from 人 and 臣, taking the sense of lying prostrate. All characters in this group are formed from 臥.

shuowen:5223.text: To look down from above. Formed from 臥, with abbreviated 䘓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5224.text: To oversee. Formed from 臥, with 品 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5225.text: Chu calls a lazy child 嬾䭆. Formed from 臥 and 食.

shuowen:5226.text: The body. Depicts a person’s body. Formed from 人, with 𠂆 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 身.

shuowen:5227.text: The body or trunk. Formed from 身, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5228.text: To return. Formed from reversed 身. All characters in this group are formed from 㐆.

shuowen:5229.text: Abundant musical performance is called 殷. Formed from 㐆 and 殳. The Changes says: “Offer it abundantly to the Lord on High.”

shuowen:5230.text: What one relies on for covering. The upper garment is 衣, the lower 裳. Depicts covering two people. All characters in this group are formed from 衣.

shuowen:5231.text: To cut and make clothing. Formed from 衣, with 𢦔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5232.text: For the Son of Heaven’s offerings to former kings, coiling dragons are embroidered on the lower panels, one dragon curling and facing upward. Formed from 衣, with 公 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5233.text: A red gauze garment. Formed from 衣, with 㠭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5234.text: A garment ornamented with pheasant feathers. Formed from 衣, with 俞 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a straight-skirted garment is called 襜褕.

shuowen:5235.text: A dark ceremonial garment. Formed from 衣, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5236.text: An upper garment. Formed from 衣 and 毛. Ancient people wore fur garments with the hair outward.

shuowen:5237.text: The inside of a garment. Formed from 衣, with 里 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5238.text: A cloth for carrying a child on the back. Formed from 衣, with 强 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5239.text: A garment collar. Formed from 衣, with 棘 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Make its waist and its collar.”

shuowen:5240.text: A collar with black-and-white patterning. Formed from 衣, with 㬥 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “A white garment with a red collar.”

shuowen:5241.text: The overlapping front of a garment. Formed from 衣, with 壬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5242.text: The garment’s overlapping front. Formed from 衣, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5243.text: The garment’s overlapping front. Formed from 衣, with 叞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5244.text: The edging of the garment front. Formed from 衣, with 疌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5245.text: Overlapping garment fronts. Formed from 衣, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5246.text: A knee covering. Formed from 衣, with 韋 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Among the queen’s garments is the 褘 robe,” meaning a painted robe.

shuowen:5247.text: The 襲衭 garment. Formed from 衣, with 夫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5248.text: A robe overlapping to the left. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 龖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5249.text: A padded robe, 襺. Formed from 衣, with 包 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Wearing a worn robe padded with old floss.”

shuowen:5250.text: A padded robe. Formed from 衣, with 繭 indicating the sound. With new floss it is 襺; with old floss, 袍. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “In high summer, double padded robes.”

shuowen:5251.text: Southern Chu calls a single-layer garment 𧝵. Formed from 衣, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5252.text: The part of a garment above the belt. Formed from 衣, with 矛 indicating the sound. Another explanation: north-south extent is 袤, east-west extent 廣.

shuowen:5253.text: Where the belt is knotted. Formed from 衣, with 會 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “A garment has its belt-knot.”

shuowen:5254.text: A hemp garment. The Odes says: “Over brocade, a hemp garment,” showing a return to ancient simplicity. Formed from 衣, with 耿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5255.text: 袛裯, a short garment. Formed from 衣, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5256.text: A garment sleeve; also 袛裯. Formed from 衣, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5257.text: A 裯 is called 襤褸; 襤 means without edging. Formed from 衣, with 監 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5258.text: A garment without sleeves is 䙃. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 惰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5259.text: The seam along a garment’s body. Formed from 衣, with 毒 indicating the sound. Read like 督.

shuowen:5260.text: A garment sleeve. Formed from 衣, with 去 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 袪 means 褱, to embrace. The cuff measures one chi two cun. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Pi cut off his sleeve.”

shuowen:5261.text: A sleeve. Formed from 衣, with 𥝩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5262.text: A sleeve. Formed from 衣, with 夬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5263.text: A sleeve. Another explanation: to conceal. Formed from 衣, with 鬼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5264.text: To hold against the sides. Formed from 衣, with 眔 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a bag.

shuowen:5265.text: To hold in the bosom. Formed from 衣, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5266.text: Clothing covering the front. Formed from 衣, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5267.text: A garment’s side slit, 衸. Formed from 衣, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5268.text: A garment’s side slit, 袥. Formed from 衣, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5269.text: Trousers. Formed from 衣, with 睪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5270.text: The skirt of a garment. Formed from 衣, with 它 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Court robes, trailing sash.”

shuowen:5271.text: A robe or garment skirt. Formed from 衣, with 居 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 居.

shuowen:5272.text: The garment 諸𧘚; its precise form is uncertain. Formed from 衣, with 于 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5273.text: Trousers. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 寒 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Levy trousers and short jackets.”

shuowen:5274.text: The legs of trousers. Formed from 衣, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5275.text: The upper part of trousers. Formed from 衣, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5276.text: A broad, large garment. Formed from 衣, with 尋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5277.text: A garment with a broad skirt. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 𠊻 indicating the sound; 𠊻 is ancient-script 𠈃.

shuowen:5278.text: Swaddling clothes. Formed from 衣, with 啻 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Then clothe him in swaddling.”

shuowen:5279.text: A garment’s full, straight width. Formed from 衣, with 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5280.text: The appearance of layered clothing. Formed from 衣, with 圍 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “䙟䙟䙡䙡,” describing layered clothing.

shuowen:5281.text: The appearance of layered clothing. Formed from 衣, with 复 indicating the sound. Another explanation: padded clothing.

shuowen:5282.text: Clothing thick, 褆褆. Formed from 衣, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5283.text: The appearance of thick clothing. Formed from 衣, with 農 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “How rich and thick that garment is.”

shuowen:5284.text: The rustling of new clothes. Another explanation: the back seam. Formed from 衣, with 叔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5285.text: A garment spread out. Formed from 衣, with 多 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The duke met the Marquis of Qi at Chi.”

shuowen:5286.text: The skirt of a garment. Formed from 衣, with 㕯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5287.text: The appearance of long clothing. Formed from 衣, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5288.text: The appearance of long clothing. Formed from 衣, with abbreviated 叀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5289.text: A short garment. Formed from 衣, with 鳥 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “There was a hollow 𧜣”; the quoted phrase is uncertain.

shuowen:5290.text: Layered clothing. Formed from 衣, with 執 indicating the sound. Ba Commandery has Diehong County, 褺虹.

shuowen:5291.text: The appearance of long clothing. Formed from 衣, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5292.text: A short garment. Formed from 衣, with 蜀 indicating the sound. Read like 蜀.

shuowen:5293.text: Clothing reaching the ground. Formed from 衣, with 斲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5294.text: A short garment. Formed from 衣, with 需 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a warm garment.

shuowen:5295.text: A small or tight garment. Formed from 衣, with 扁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5296.text: Clothing without floss padding. Formed from 衣, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5297.text: Clothing without a second layer. Formed from 衣, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5298.text: Han ordinances call taking off one’s clothing to plow 襄. Formed from 衣, with 𤕦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5299.text: A sleeping cover, one and a half body-lengths long. Formed from 衣, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5300.text: A large quilt. Formed from 衣, with 今 indicating the sound.
